claims.text: Atomic size mismatches create heterogeneous lattice distortions in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Heterogeneous lattice distortions produce local variations in bonding strength.
Local variations in bonding strength govern dislocation motion and mechanical behavior.
Local variations in bonding strength govern electron–phonon interactions and thermoelastic behavior.
Rapid solidification leaves conventionally processed as-cast refractory HEAs with significant lattice distortion.
A recovery anneal conducted without full recrystallization can reduce local heterogeneous lattice distortions while leaving overall composition unchanged.
Spatial variations in lattice strain locally alter bonding stiffness.
Spatial variations in lattice strain locally alter dislocation mobility.
Annealing relaxes local atomic misfits and thereby reduces heterogeneous lattice distortion.
Reduced heterogeneous lattice distortion lowers obstacles to dislocation motion.
Lower obstacles to dislocation motion reduce yield strength.
Relaxation of lattice distortion reduces strain-rate sensitivity.
Relaxation of lattice distortion makes electron–phonon coupling more spatially uniform.
More uniform electron–phonon coupling moderates spatial variations in thermoelastic coefficients.
Relative to the as-cast control, annealed samples will have a statistically significant decrease in yield strength.
Relative to the as-cast control, annealed samples may have less pronounced strain-rate sensitivity.
Relative to the as-cast control, annealed samples will show reduced variability in elastic modulus as a function of temperature.
Testing in an inert atmosphere avoids oxidation during high-temperature mechanical testing.
A comparison is interpretable as a lattice-distortion test only if annealing does not cause recrystallization or unwanted phase changes.
